title: Checking whether RAG answers are supported

asked.text: Make a table comparing how the detection papers in my library decide a claim is unsupported: method, what it needs (labels, a second model, access to internals), and where it was tested.

report:
These six papers in your library decide whether a RAG answer is supported in three ways: the model judges its own output, a separate judge reads the answer against the retrieved context, or a probe reads the generator's internals. They differ more in what they need to run than in how they decide, and none is tested against the others on the same outputs.

## The model judges itself

[Asai et al. 2023](owlit://library/arxiv-2310.11511) train the generator to emit critique tokens as it writes, learned from a critic that GPT-4 labelled offline. [Manakul et al. 2023](owlit://library/arxiv-2303.08896) need no training at all: they sample several answers and treat the facts the samples disagree on as likely made up. SelfCheckGPT is the only paper here that needs neither labels nor access to the model, but it was tested on text written without retrieval.

## A separate judge reads the answer against the context

[Es et al. 2023](owlit://library/arxiv-2309.15217) prompt an LLM to judge whether each statement of an answer can be inferred from the context, with no reference answers. [Saad-Falcon et al. 2023](owlit://library/arxiv-2311.09476) fine-tune small judges on synthetic data and correct their scores with a few hundred human labels. [Kovács & Recski 2025](owlit://library/arxiv-2502.17125) drop the LLM judge for a token classifier trained on RAGTruth that marks the unsupported spans. Ragas and ARES score a whole system; LettuceDetect marks the words of one answer.

## Reading the generator's internals

[Sun et al. 2024](owlit://library/arxiv-2410.11414) weigh how much the copying heads draw on the retrieved text against how much the FFN layers add from the model's own memory. It needs labels and white-box access to the generator, the most of any paper here.

## What it means for your related work

The three families are the three lines of your related-work paragraph, and the gap it names holds: nothing here runs a critique token, a sampling check and an internal probe on the same RAG answers. RAGTruth is the one dataset two of them share (LettuceDetect and ReDeEP), which makes it the natural ground for that comparison. For Ragas, ARES and LettuceDetect this rests on their abstracts.

## Read first

[Manakul et al. 2023](owlit://library/arxiv-2303.08896), the simplest check and the one the others have to beat; [Sun et al. 2024](owlit://library/arxiv-2410.11414), the only one that says why an answer that looks supported goes wrong; [Kovács & Recski 2025](owlit://library/arxiv-2502.17125), for RAGTruth.
